entries.3075cc2786d42fbe: Businesses including sensing and devices, logistics, welfare services and real estate leasing. Because the securities report describes this category as business segments and the like not included in the reportable segments, it is placed last regardless of the size of its revenue. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥6,867 million (up 12.9% year on year), and operating profit was ¥1,972 million (up 35.4%). Subsidiaries including Anritsu Devices Co., Ltd., Anritsu Kosan Co., Ltd. and Anritsu Real Estate Co., Ltd. handle the manufacture of the Company's products, logistics services, real estate leasing and similar activities.
entries.3aab41af5e96687c: A measuring instrument manufacturer based in Atsugi, Kanagawa Prefecture, that makes and sells mainly electronic measuring instruments for telecommunications, as well as inspection equipment for food factories and testing equipment for EVs.
entries.45b96a6ba7138bfa: A reportable segment that makes and sells test equipment for EVs and batteries, power measuring instruments and data acquisition systems, and monitoring solutions for video surveillance of roads, dams, rivers and similar sites. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥10,787 million (up 26.2% year on year), accounting for 9% of consolidated revenue, and operating profit was ¥850 million (down 5.5%). Takasago, Ltd. provides test equipment for EV drivetrains and batteries, drawing on its strength in power supply systems, and DEWETRON GmbH of Austria, all of whose shares were acquired on October 21, 2025, has been included in the scope of consolidation since November, during the third quarter. The securities report states that revenue increased because DEWETRON GmbH was consolidated, while profit decreased because, in demand for EV and battery testing in Japan, customer investment was delayed against the background of U.S. tariff policy and an adjustment phase in EV investment.
entries.46fa007c143ee9d6: A reportable segment that makes and sells measuring instruments for digital communications and IP networks, for optical communications, for mobile communications, and general-purpose RF, microwave and millimeter-wave measuring instruments, as well as service assurance. Of the 3 reportable segments, it has the largest revenue from external customers. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥68,774 million (down 1.9% year on year), accounting for 59% of consolidated revenue, and operating profit was ¥10,782 million (up 28.7%). The securities report states that this business is divided into 3 sub-segments serving the "network infrastructure market," the "mobile market" and the "electronics market." In addition to the Company's own manufacturing and sales, Tohoku Anritsu Co., Ltd. manufactures the Company's products, and sales subsidiaries in the United States, Europe, Asia and elsewhere sell and maintain the Company's products. The securities report states that customer investment, which had been delayed by U.S. tariff policy, recovered and demand related to data centers was strong, but revenue fell because the first-quarter decline could not be recovered, while profitability improved through reduced inventories and cost control.
